title: model-map
description: The dispatch-time routing registry (ADR-032 §3, shaped by ADR-035). Validated by cli/internal/harness/model_map.go, which reads THIS FILE rather than restating its rules — so the contract lives here and only its interpreter lives in Go. Adding a keyword here requires implementing it there; an unimplemented keyword is a loud error, never a silent pass.

$comment.description: The measured rationale. Policy registries in this repo carry it because the reasoning is the artifact — reviewer-pool.json's $comment is the only record of why its fallback order is what it is.

version.description: Two consumer classes read this file at different cadences — the render engine resolves `tiers` at compile time, a dispatcher resolves `chains` at run time — and that is the drift this field exists for.

pools.description: Inference pools. A pool is a quota, not a tool: `nan` is a pool, `pi` is a harness that reaches it.

concurrency.description: Level 1 declaration only. NOTHING decrements this today — a dispatcher would, and there is none. Declaring it makes the budget legible, which is more than existed before; it does not make it enforced.

probe.description: How to answer 'is this pool reachable HERE'. `env:NAME` or `bin:NAME`. The map declares what can exist; the probe answers whether it does on this machine.

harnesses.description: Agent runtimes. Each names the pools it can reach — and every name must resolve in `pools`, which is the rule x-poolReferencesResolve enforces and a stock schema cannot express.

tiers.description: Neutral tier -> a model id per harness. Resolved at COMPILE time and fed into each harness's native render.

chains.description: Ordered fallback per tier, as `pool:model`. Resolved at RUN time and read only by a level-2 dispatcher: a Claude Task cannot fail over to NaN, so cross-pool fallback exists only outside the session. Kept separate from reviewer-pool.json deliberately — that one ranks independence above availability, this one ranks availability. ADR-035 states the merge trigger: a third consumer needing an ordered chain.

services.description: Non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank). They are provider surfaces the map is responsible for, and they fit neither tiers nor chains.
